title: Amortized Simulation-Based Inference in Generalized Bayes via Neural Posterior Estimation
claim: Across benchmarks and temperatures, one amortized estimator's route variants track or beat per-setting baselines on two-sample metrics, though not uniformly.
layout: 4x4 grid of line plots, rows are benchmarks, shared bottom legend
description: A 4-by-4 grid of line plots with a shared legend at the bottom. Rows are the four benchmarks: Gaussian Mixture, Two Moons, SLCP and Lorenz96, labeled at the left. Columns alternate between two metrics, c2st and mmd, each at two dataset sizes (n=10000 and n=100000). The x-axis is the temperature beta, running from about 0.1 to 1.5. Each panel has five colored lines with markers: NLE (blue circles), NRE (orange squares), RouteA_NPE (green triangles), RouteB_NLE (red diamonds) and RouteB_NRE (purple stars). Curves are noisy and cross each other. In the Lorenz96 row they rise smoothly with beta. Some mmd panels are clipped at the axis ceiling. No single method wins everywhere, so the eye goes to the dense, repeated line plots.
caption: Route A/B comparison across benchmarks with a shared legend.
abstract: Generalized Bayesian Inference (GBI) tempers a loss with a temperature $Î²> 0$ to mitigate overconfidence and improve robustness under model misspecification, but existing GBI methods typically rely on costly MCMC or SDE-based samplers and must be re-run for each new dataset and each $Î²$ value. We give the first fully amortized variational approximation for the tempered posterior family by training a single data- and $Î²$-conditioned neural posterior estimator that enables sampling in a single forward pass, without simulator calls or inference-time MCMC. We introduce two complementary training routes: one synthesizes off-manifold samples from the tempered joint distribution, and the other reweights a fixed base dataset using self-normalized importance sampling (SNIS). We show that the SNIS-weighted objective provides a consistent forward-KL fit to the tempered posterior with finite weight variance. Across four standard simulation-based inference benchmarks, including the chaotic Lorenz-96 system, our $Î²$-amortized estimator achieves competitive posterior approximations, in standard two-sample metrics, matching non-amortized MCMC-based power-posterior samplers over a wide range of temperatures.
